now: Currently: ESnet (remote) · just published PEARC '26 · teaching the NRP on the side

about.description: I'm a research networking systems engineer at ESnet, the Energy Sciences Network at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. I work on the software-defined networks and transfer tooling that keep high-energy physics data moving at petabyte scale.
details: My path ran through San Diego first: at the San Diego Supercomputer Center (UCSD) I worked on all sorts of things: the National Research Platform's Kubernetes substrate and its FABRIC integration, the SENSE Kubernetes operator, segment routing on FPGAs, CUDA tooling, Prometheus exporters for novel chips, and P4 with machine learning on SmartNICs.

In August 2026 I joined ESnet at LBNL as a research networking systems engineer, remotely, from the same city I've been in. The fun part is data movement: software-defined networking for high-energy physics, SENSE orchestration, and interop between the tools scientists use to move files.

Off the clock I keep a long-lived list of side projects, network tooling, ML experiments, and the occasional impossible project, and I unironically believe every big idea deserves a small weekend prototype.
